title: Street-Tree Site Capacity Tool — V1 Rules
purpose: Translate reviewed source rules and explicit project interpretations into machine-readable operations while preserving unresolved issues and V1 boundaries.

rule_statuses.active: May be executed automatically in V1 when required inputs are known.
rule_statuses.conditional: May be applied only when stated source or project conditions are satisfied.
rule_statuses.reference_only: Source-supported information retained for context or later automation; V1 does not automatically judge it.
rule_statuses.unresolved: The reviewed source does not support a complete automated interpretation. Do not infer the missing relationship.

global_guardrails: Never convert UNKNOWN into a factual value without evidence.
Never present DESIGN_ASSUMPTION as SOURCE_RULE or CITY_DATA.
Do not infer existing qualifying soil geometry from tree coordinates or inventory data.
Do not treat a soil-volume benchmark as complete City approval or complete site suitability.
Do not silently resolve Shared / Row scaling.
Do not infer a species-to-Columnar mapping without explicit source support.
Do not invent a soil-cell credit factor.
Do not assume a curb position, a soil depth or an existing open-strip width; they are knobs or designer inputs, never defaults.
Utility positions are plan positions only; never imply a utility depth is known.

rules.name: Block-face band share (per-tree apportioning of one continuous boulevard band)
rules.formula: soil_area_m2 = band width × tributary length; share_m3 = soil_area_m2 × soil_depth_m (R05) × credit (R06/R07)

definitions.block_face: the boulevard on one side of the street between two cross streets (City block outline frontage), treated as one continuous soil band
definitions.band_width: front boulevard width from R30: property line → curb face, minus the Table 8-3 sidewalk clear width and the Table 8-4 back boulevard for the chosen land use, minus the 0.15 m curb; measured on the perpendicular through each tree; the existing state uses the designer's open-strip width instead
definitions.tributary_length: interior tree: midpoint to the west neighbour to midpoint to the east neighbour; end-of-row tree: the outer half equals the inner half (symmetric cell), cut back to the band / segment end if that is nearer; a lone tree in a segment: symmetric about the tree to the nearer segment end
definitions.planting_condition: two or more trees on the face → shared_row (Table 9-2 Shared / Row column); a lone tree on its face → solitary

source_reference.document: City of Vancouver Engineering Design Manual
passages: 9.3.3.1: boulevard width is a fundamental design parameter that governs tree size, spacing, long-term health
9.3.3.1: protect continuous linear space for trees aligned with the centre of boulevards
Table 9-2: Shared / Row of Trees column and average spacing

guardrails: The per-tree apportioning is a project interpretation (08_redefinition §2.4); the source gives a per-tree Shared / Row value and no scaling method, so R21 stays unresolved and is reported alongside every block-face result.
Spacing is measured; the tool never proposes a spacing.
The solitary-column comparison is retained for every selected tree.

The band is the front boulevard (EDM §8.4.6): between back of curb and sidewalk. Soil under the sidewalk or back boulevard is outside the design band; native soil under hardscape counts only if tested (GRI p.18, R29).
measured_inputs: curb knob (curb face from the centreline)
land use category (Table 8-3 row) and width level for R30
rules.notes: schema_inputs is empty on purpose: the inputs are geometry measured outside the record by src/block_face.py and listed in the trace; keeping them out of schema_inputs prevents the scenario mechanism from treating measured fields as downstream of themselves.

rules.name: Utility interruption of the soil band (GRI qualifying condition + Table 2-2 tree clearances)

water_main.source: Table 2-2, City Water Infrastructure: 'Minimum 2.0m clearance from trees'

sewer_main.source: Table 2-2, City Sewer Infrastructure: 'Minimum 2.0m clearance from trees'

sewer_catch_basin.source: Table 2-2, City Sewer Infrastructure 'including … catchbasins and catchbasin leads': 'Minimum 2.0m clearance from trees'

electrical_conduit.source: Table 2-2, City Electrical Infrastructure: 'The minimum clearance between edge of tree trunk and conduits shall be 0.3m'

street_lighting_pole.source: Table 2-2 gives 0.3 m from pole bases for utilities and 1.5 m at intersections for signal poles; no clearance from trees is stated

documents.passage: The soil that contributes to a given trees soil volume requirement must be directly adjacent to the tree and not interrupted by any utility conflicts.

documents.document: City of Vancouver Engineering Design Manual

interpretation.strip: each utility within the band (or within its clearance of the band) removes a strip of the band: the bounding extent of the utility inside the band grown by the clearance on every side (PROJECT_INTERPRETATION: a Table 2-2 tree clearance read as a soil-band interruption width)
interpretation.crossing: a strip spanning the full band width splits the band into segments; tributary lengths are recomputed inside each segment
interpretation.partial: a strip not spanning the full width removes band width on its length, on the far side of the tree
interpretation.tree_inside_strip: the tree itself lies within the clearance: share not computed, utility_conflict = conflict_confirmed with status REVIEW_REQUIRED; the tool does not judge the existing condition

guardrails: Applying a Table 2-2 tree clearance as a band interruption width is a project interpretation and is labelled as such in every result.
City utility layers give plan position only (catch basins 'location approximate'); depth is never inferred.
Service connections and third-party utilities are not in the City layers; absence of an interruption is not a clearance certificate.
Designer-entered utilities are USER_INPUT (typed) or CONFIRMED_SITE_DATA (evidence reference required) and are drawn in that grade.
measured_inputs: City utility layers listed in city_datasets (plan position)
the band rectangle and per-tree cells from R26

rules.name: Existing soil credit default: open planting strip only, hardscape-covered native soil excluded unless tested

source_reference.document: Vancouver GRI Planting Guidelines
passages: native soil underneath the hardscape surrounding the GI system should generally not be considered as contributing to the required soil volume for the tree
Native fill may be considered acceptable soil volume for trees if tests are conducted that demonstrate that the soil has acceptable properties … and is not excessively compacted

rules.notes: Existing-state default: only the open planting strip counts toward existing credited volume; its width, depth and type are designer inputs in two grades (USER_INPUT typed / CONFIRMED_SITE_DATA with evidence). No 'typical Vancouver boulevard depth' exists in this tool; with no depth the existing share is UNKNOWN.
guardrails: Never default the existing strip width, depth or soil type.
A typed (USER_INPUT) existing value yields a result phrased 'based on your inputs' and drawn hatched; only CONFIRMED_SITE_DATA is drawn solid.
Soil under sidewalk or road is not credited in the existing state; a design state may propose soil there under R06–R11.
measured_inputs: designer's existing open-strip width, depth and soil type (two grades)

rules.name: Front boulevard band width from the pedestrian-realm cross-section (Table 8-3 sidewalk, Table 8-4 back boulevard, 0.15 m curb)
measured_inputs: land use category chosen by the user (Table 8-3 row)
width level: constrained / minimum / preferred (default minimum)
rules.formula: boulevard_width_m = (property line - curb face) - sidewalk_clear_width_m[land_use][level] - back_boulevard_width_m[table_8_4_row][level] - curb_width_m

residential_detached.table_8_3: Residential or Industrial (detached, duplex, multiplex, townhouse)

commercial_mixed_use.preferred_note: depends on volume (Table 8-3); UNKNOWN in this tool

source_reference.document: City of Vancouver Engineering Design Manual
passages: p.253 §8.4.3.1: The pedestrian realm is the publicly accessible space between the back of curb and the property line … sidewalks, which provide clear space for walking; and front and back boulevards, which provide space for trees, utilities, and street furniture.
p.253 Table 8-3 note 2: Significant work should be made to retain trees in the front boulevard.

p.255 §8.4.6: Front boulevards, also referred to as utility strips or tree boulevards, are located between the back of curb or pavement edge and the sidewalk … Where widths are constrained, front boulevards take precedence over back boulevards.
p.256 Table 8-4 note 6: For street trees, achieving the minimum front boulevard should be prioritized over the minimum back boulevard.
p.256 Table 8-4 note 7: Boulevard widths exclude curb widths, which is currently an additional 0.15m.

guardrails: Land use is a category the user chooses from the Table 8-3 rows; it is never inferred from zoning, address or building data, and it is not a numeric knob.
The width level (constrained / minimum / preferred) applies to both tables at once; 'minimum' is the default reading and is stated in every result.
Composing the two tables and the curb width into one band width is a PROJECT_INTERPRETATION; each width is SOURCE_RULE and is cited with its page.
The derived front boulevard is compared with the Table 8-4 front-boulevard column as reference information only; no verdict.
A band of zero or negative width is reported as such; the tool does not shrink the sidewalk or back boulevard to make room.

rules.name: Engineered-soil extension zones beyond the front boulevard (fifth lever)
rules.formula: share_total_m3 = band credited_soil_volume_m3 + Σ zone credited_soil_volume_m3 (KNOWN zones only)

definitions.zone: a rectangle of engineered soil the designer draws adjacent to the front boulevard: side 'property' (from the sidewalk edge toward the property line, under the sidewalk and back boulevard) or side 'road' (from the back of curb toward the centreline, under the curb and parking lane); one zone per side; clipped at the property line / centreline
definitions.connectivity: zone soil counts only where it is still connected to the tree's band cell after the Table 2-2 interruption strips (R28) are applied to band + zones together (GRI p.18: directly adjacent, not interrupted)
definitions.crediting: each zone is evaluated as its own record with its own soil_type, depth and provenance: native_soil under hardscape only when CONFIRMED_SITE_DATA with evidence (R29, GRI p.18), structural_soil 50 % (R06) and only for a new tree (R08), soil_cell never yields a number (R11) and lists the R10 manual conditions, other stays unresolved (R25)
definitions.tree_state: a zone that needs a new tree (R08/R09) is credited only when the design is run as vacant_replacement (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION); for the existing tree it is REFUSED with the passage

source_reference.document: Vancouver GRI Planting Guidelines
passages: directly adjacent to the tree and not interrupted
native soil underneath the hardscape ... should generally not be considered

source_reference.document: City of Vancouver Engineering Design Manual
passages: only permissible when installing new trees

guardrails: Summing zone shares with the band share is a project interpretation, reported as DERIVED_CALCULATION with R31 in the trace; the source gives per-tree volumes, not a composition rule.
Zones are always drawn hatched (design assumption) unless CONFIRMED_SITE_DATA; they never change the band, the spacing or the Table 9-2 benchmark.
A zone never yields a credited value for soil_type = soil_cell or other.
Depth in a zone is the designer's number; the tool does not know what is under the sidewalk or the road beyond the City utility plan positions.
rules.notes: R31 extension zones: engineered soil drawn beyond the front boulevard, credited per zone by the existing crediting rules and added to the band share (PROJECT_INTERPRETATION).

rules.name: Tree protection barrier distance by trunk diameter (By-law 9958 Schedule A; reference only)
rules.lookup_rule: trunk diameter measured 1.4 m above grade (By-law §1.2 'protection barrier' (b), §2.2); the distance of the smallest Schedule A row at or above the diameter; below 20 cm the By-law does not apply (§2.2 exemption for small trees, except replacement trees and hedges); above 100 cm the last row (6.0 m) is reported with a note. Standard Detail G10.1 draws the same requirement as '6 × trunk Ø measured at 1.4 m height' parallel to the curb.

boulevard_offsets_m.cite: By-law 9958 §7.8(c)(iii)–(iv) p.15; Street Tree Guidelines 2011 p.19; Standard Detail G10.1 section A-A

guardrails: A protection barrier distance is a construction-site requirement (where a fence must stand before demolition, excavation or construction), not a root extent: it is drawn as a dashed ring around the trunk labelled 'protection radius (By-law 9958 Sch. A), not root extent' and never changes any credited volume or share.
The engine reports it in reference_info from the City's inventory_diameter (CITY_DATA); it is never applied to the record.
The By-law measures the barrier parallel to the curb; across the boulevard the barrier is bounded by the curb (0.6 m) and the sidewalk edge (0.3 m), so the drawn ring is cut at those lines.

source_reference.document: City of Vancouver Protection of Trees By-law No. 9958 (consolidated to December 9, 2025; amended to include By-law 14546 effective January 1, 2026)

revision_notes: Round 1.1: added R25 so soil_type = other produces an explicit unresolved crediting state instead of a silent UNKNOWN.

Round 8 (08_redefinition_2026-09-22): added R26 block-face band share, R27 Shared / Row classes under the per-tree reading, R28 utility interruption (GRI p.18 + Table 2-2), R29 existing-credit default (GRI p.18); source basis extended with 02b, 02c and 08; two global guardrails on knobs and utility depth.
Round 8 step 2 (2026-09-24): band = front boulevard. R30 added from EDM §8.4 pp.253–256 (02d); R26 definitions updated (front boulevard band, symmetric end-of-row cells).

Phase 3 (2026-09-28, 11_redefinition §8): added R31 extension zones (the fifth lever): designer-drawn engineered-soil rectangles beyond the front boulevard on the property or road side, credited per zone by R06/R07/R08/R09/R10/R11/R25/R29 and summed with the band share; design may be run as vacant_replacement (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION) so that R08/R09 eligibility can be tested for a new tree.

Phase 4 (2026-09-28, 11_redefinition §6): R17 re-scoped from unresolved (SOURCE_GAP) to reference_only lookup: the engine reads Table 9-3 (12_species_table_9-3.json) for the record's genus / species / cultivar and reports the listed class in reference_info; target_tree_class is never set by it. Version 1.3.

Night of 2026-09-28 (task 0.5 / 3): added R32, the By-law 9958 Schedule A protection-barrier distance by trunk diameter, as a reference_only lookup from inventory_diameter (CITY_DATA). It is drawn as a protection radius beside the nominal roots and labelled as such; it is never a root extent and never enters a share. Version 1.4.
